correctness.rationale: For n>=3, m>=2 in K_1 vee(P_n[K_m]), verified terminal cliques are simplicial and entirely forced; hub h is covered by a shortest end-to-end path, so never in a minimal geodetic set. Diameter 2 and the neighborhood geometry give the exact per-interior-layer feasibility s_i=m or (s_(i-1)>0 and s_(i+1)>0). Deletion tests leave exactly full F, empty Z, singleton P and the three stated nearest-neighbor conditions; no multi-vertex partial layer is minimal. Pair-state 9x9 transfer weights v(F)=z^m, v(Z)=1, v(P)=mz count labelled sets without quotienting; explicit witness words and small exceptional enumeration prove purity only n=3 or m=2,n=4,6. Independently constructed graph distances and all geodetic vertex closures for n=3..5,m=2 and n=3..4,m=3, matching the transfer values. General proof is local, not reliant on finite tests.
residual_risks: Independent brute force is for small complete clique layers only; uniform proof for arbitrary n,m depends on the verified local geodesic/deletion characterization.

value.rationale: Clique substitution and joining a universal hub produce a natural diameter-two family whose minimal geodetic sets have a nontrivial local combinatorial classification. The weighted 9x9 transfer matrix counts all labelled minimal sets, and the sporadic pure complex at six doubleton layers is a sharp, mathematically motivated boundary. These are exact invariants researchers may need beyond the scalar geodetic number and beyond a black-box enumerator.
